turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I feel like my body’s been kind of out of my control. For a while I was just pacing around my apartment all night, making notes for this supper-club idea, like I couldn’t stop moving. And now lately it’s the opposite — I’m so slowed down my sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on.

symptom_reasoning.S028: The patient reports a period of inability to stop pacing followed by marked slowing in daily movement, consistent with psychomotor agitation and retardation.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During that time when you were pacing all night and felt unable to stop, did you hear or see things that other people couldn’t?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think so. I wasn’t hearing voices or seeing things, at least not that I noticed. I was just really wired and couldn’t settle down.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that others could not.

turns.doctor_question: During that wired period, did you feel unusually powerful or important?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… I did. I really thought I was onto something huge with this bilingual supper club idea. Like, I honestly believed it was going to be the best one in the city, and that investors would be dumb not to put money into it — even though I didn’t actually have a job or any money lined up.

symptom_reasoning.S035: Patient endorses feeling unusually important and expresses grandiose confidence that the unsupported supper club idea would be the best in the city and that investors would be foolish not to fund it.

turns.doctor_question: During that wired time, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. After I got fired, I felt… weirdly unstoppable, like excited in a way that didn’t really fit what was happening. But it also wasn’t just happy — if anyone questioned my plans or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry, like they were trying to ruin my life.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient endorses feeling unusually excited and unstoppable after being fired, with marked irritability and anger when others questioned or slowed their plans.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had low times, but I don’t know if it was most of the day almost every day like that. I’d have to think about it.

turns.doctor_question: During that wired period, were you hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure how to answer that… I don’t think I was hospitalized, no. At least, not that I remember.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices when you were not feeling especially high, energized, or depressed?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really sure what would count as hearing voices, but I haven’t noticed that happening when I wasn’t already in some kind of mood state.

turns.doctor_question: During that wired period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like getting into major trouble at work, with money, or with other people?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. It caused a lot of problems. I couldn’t keep work plans straight, and I was messing up stuff with rent and things I’d promised my family I’d do. It got to the point where my sister had to take me to a crisis clinic because I just couldn’t get basic responsibilities organized on my own.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient reports being unable to keep work plans, rent arrangements, and basic responsibilities organized.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. It’s been more than two weeks — honestly, the heavy, slowed-down feeling has been going on for about three months now, most days.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient confirms feeling depressed or down most days for approximately three months.
symptom_reasoning.S028: The patient describes a persistent slowed-down feeling, supporting psychomotor slowing.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d call it sad the whole time. It’s more like feeling down and heavy most days, yeah, but I don’t know if it’s every day or all day.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes feeling down and heavy on most days, supporting depressed mood despite uncertainty about whether it occurs all day or every day.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. Things I usually like—cooking, taking food pictures, listening to music, playing pickup soccer, even volunteering—just feel kind of flat now. I know I used to care about them, but I can’t really make myself feel interested.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient reports that previously enjoyable activities now feel flat and that they cannot feel interested in them.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know if I’d say “depressed” most of the day nearly every day. I’ve been feeling really down and heavy a lot, but it’s hard for me to pin down exactly how much of the day or how many days.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I have anything clear to say about that right now.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear answer for that right now.

turns.doctor_question: During that wired period, did you need much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I don’t think I paid close enough attention to my sleep then to say if it was much less than usual.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you felt hopeless?
turns.patient_response: I don’t know. I mean, I’ve had rough days, but I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I haven’t really thought about it that way.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you felt tired or like you had very little energy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. I’ve been really tired. I can sleep most of the morning and still feel heavy, like my arms and legs are full of wet sand. Even walking to the bus or washing dishes can feel like too much.

symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient explicitly reports being really tired despite sleeping most of the morning, with heavy limbs and low energy making routine activities feel difficult.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. I’ll open job applications or the rent page and then just sit there staring at it. I reread the same line over and over, and then I kind of forget what I was even trying to do. Decisions feel really hard.

symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient describes repeatedly rereading application or rent-page text, forgetting their intended task, and finding decisions very difficult.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. My sister’s noticed it. Lately I’ve been moving really slow, like it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. It’s weird, because before that I was kind of the opposite—pacing around the apartment all night making notes and stuff. But now I feel really slowed down, like my body isn’t doing what I want.

symptom_reasoning.S028: The patient confirms that her sister has noticed she has recently been moving very slowly, describing taking a long time to put on shoes and feeling physically slowed down.

turns.doctor_question: During these past three months, has your appetite been noticeably different than usual?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it’s been different. Some days I barely eat at all—just coffee or maybe a tortilla—because food just tastes like cardboard. And my jeans have been fitting looser, even though I’m not trying to lose weight.

symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient reports markedly reduced intake on some days, food tasting unappealing, and unintentionally looser-fitting jeans, indicating appetite and likely weight change.
